newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity trades lower with warm weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity trades lower with warm weather.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading lower Tuesday with some weakness from warm weather in the U.S. West and discussion of ample hydroelectric supplies, industry sources said.
As of 1300 EST, February California Oregon Border (COB) was trading down 32 cents at $13.15 after exchanges in a range of $13.00-13.25 per megawatt hour (MWh).
March COB had traded down 10 cents at $11.40 after hitting a new contract low of $11.35 per MWh.

February Palo Verde (PV) had traded down 54 cents at $15.25 after trades as low as $15.05, while March PV was down 20 cents at $13.50 and April was down 20 cents at a new contract low of $13.10 per MWh.
Warm weather in the U.S. West was dampening power demand, and forecasts called for above and much above normal temperatures through the West to the end of January.
Separately, a 500 kilvolt transmission line, which runs from Snohomish County, Wash. to the Canadian border, could stay shut until later this week after damage from an ice storm late last week.
The outage of the 350 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Comanche coal-fired power plant in Pueblo, Colorado, was extended for more time to repair damages from a fire in mid-December.
NYMEX said as of 1230 EST an estimated total of 84 COB and 114 PV contracts had traded.
COB open interest for Jan 20 fell 20 to 3,346 while PV open interest fell one to 1,390, NYMEX said.
